items.headline: Federal appeals court rules migrants must get real notice before third-country deportation
items.summary: The First Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston ruled that immigration officials must give detainees meaningful notice and a chance to contest being deported to a country where they have no ties. The ruling largely upholds a lower court decision that found the policy unlawful.
items.why_it_matters: It reinforces due process protections for migrants against a policy that had sent deportees to countries thousands of miles from their homeland.
